messages:
jordan-acmecorp: Hey team — our users hit a bunch of Google SSO logins failing this morning. 403 on the callback, says state mismatch. Happening only when we route through our staging proxy (internal).

amanda.cs: Thanks, jordan. Can you paste the full callback URL you see in the browser/network console when the redirect fails? Also which client_id (prod/stage)? :thinking:

jordan-acmecorp: client_id: acme-redwood-stage. Here's the redirect URL we get from the provider: 
`https://auth.acme.example.com:8443/oauth2/callback?code=4/abcDEF&state=Tt%2Bq%2B3%3D`
Error in app: `403 state_mismatch` after the code is returned and we do token exchange. Works fine if user hits the origin URL (no proxy) or when I test locally on :443. Only fails via the proxy.

tariq-engineering: @jordan-acmecorp thanks — two quick suspects: 1) proxy normalizes/strips port or rewrites redirect_uri when forwarding to the app; 2) '+' or '%2B' getting converted to space or dropped — state param can be altered by intermediate layers. Can you capture the callback request that reaches your app (raw query string)?

jordan-acmecorp: attached (pasted): 
```
GET /oauth2/callback?code=4/abcDEF&state=Tt q 3= HTTP/1.1
Host: auth.acme.example.com
X-Forwarded-Proto: https
X-Forwarded-For: 35.45.12.1
X-Forwarded-Port: 443
Cookie: session=...; _oauth_state=Tt%2Bq%2B3%3D;
```
Note: the query shows spaces where there should be `+` and the Host header is `auth.acme.example.com` (no :8443). Proxy is rewriting X-Forwarded-Port to 443.

samir-identity: This looks like URL-decoding/normalization by the proxy. Important: Google requires the redirect_uri you exchange with to exactly match the authorized redirect URI registered (including port). If your app expects `https://auth.acme.example.com:8443/oauth2/callback` but the provider returns `https://auth.acme.example.com/oauth2/callback` (no port) or the proxy drops/changes the query, our state check will fail.

amanda.cs: Quick troubleshooting steps: 
- Confirm the redirect_uri registered in Google Cloud Console exactly matches what the app uses (scheme, host, port, path, trailing slash).
- Capture the request as it arrives at the app (not what the browser shows).
- Check proxy logs/config for `normalize_uri` or `merge_slashes` style settings and any URL decoding of `+` to space.

tariq-engineering: Some immediate mitigations you can try while we investigate: 
- Shorten the `state` (avoid characters that require %2B encoding) or use base64url encoding (no `+`/`/`/`=`).
- Ensure the proxy preserves the raw query and doesn't perform an extra decode/encode cycle.
- If you control the proxy, set it to forward the original `Host`+`Port` and `X-Forwarded-Port` correctly, or set `proxy_set_header Host $http_host;` in nginx so the port is retained.

jordan-acmecorp: Tried the base64url option and workaround: encode state without `+`. That fixed immediate repro, but still want root cause — our engineers say the proxy team rolled a config change late last night.

samir-identity: Also check SameSite cookie handling for auth state storage — if you store `state` in a cookie and the proxy/fronting domain changes, cookies might get dropped leading to mismatch. In your pasted headers the cookie still had encoded state, but your app is reading query state as decoded with spaces which doesn't match cookie.

amanda.cs: Can you share the proxy type? (nginx, envoy, cloudflared, kubernetes ingress, Cloudflare Worker?)

jordan-acmecorp: It's an Envoy layer in front of the app; they pushed a filter that rewrites URLs for path-based routing.

tariq-engineering: Envoy has `decode_headers` behavior for query params depending on filters. There's a known edge where `+` becomes space when intermediate decoding happens. Ask the proxy team to enable `preserve_query_string` and avoid double-decoding. Also check if the filter is rewriting the `Host` header and dropping the port — when Google redirects back, the app must use the same redirect_uri in the token exchange call as was registered. If your token exchange uses the incoming Host header (without port), you'll mismatch with Google's expectation.

amanda.cs: Next steps for support: 
1) Please ask proxy team to roll back the rewrite filter or adjust to preserve `+` encoding.
2) Update google redirect URI to include exact port if you plan to keep port in the public URL, OR configure proxy to forward the original port.
3) We'll keep monitoring — if you want, we can also temporarily relax state validation to log both values (only for a short window) to capture diff. Don't leave it relaxed in prod. :no_entry_sign:

jordan-acmecorp: I'll ping the proxy team and try the base64url short-state as a hotfix. One more thing — when the app exchanges the code we get `invalid_grant` sometimes after the 403. Could that be the PKCE verifier getting truncated?

samir-identity: Yes — if the PKCE `code_verifier` was stored client-side (cookie/local storage) and the proxy changes cookies or truncates headers, the server-side compare can fail -> `invalid_grant`. Look for header size or cookie size limits on the proxy. Envoy may be chunking large cookies. Also check any WAF rules that might be stripping `=` or `+`.

amanda.cs: TL;DR checklist I posted to support ticket: 
- Capture raw callback request at app (full query string).
- Check proxy rewrite filters for double-decoding and Host/Port preservation.
- Try base64url encode for `state` and PKCE verifier temporarily.
- Confirm authorized redirect URI in Google console exactly matches (include port).
- Watch for cookie truncation / SameSite issues.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-8721 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to amanda.cs and tariq-engineering.

jordan-acmecorp: Thanks — I'll update when proxy team responds. :thumbsup:

amanda.cs: If you can, paste a minimal nginx/envoy config snippet from the proxy team and we can point out the offending lines quickly.

tariq-engineering: Also send the token exchange error body (full response) if you still see `invalid_grant` so we can correlate.

jordan-acmecorp: Will do. Appreciate the fast help.

amanda.cs: No problem — we're on it. :white_check_mark:
